newsitem.title: USA: Clinton seeks money to improve U.S. economic data.
newsitem.headline: Clinton seeks money to improve U.S. economic data.

text.p: The White House on Thursday asked for money to improve U.S. economic statistics, saying their reputation has suffered as cash-strapped federal agencies have struggled to keep pace with a changing economy.

"Rapid changes in our economy and society, coupled with limited resources to enable the statistical agencies to keep pace with these changes, have eroded the relevance and the reputation of the statistical system," the White House said in its budget proposal for fiscal year 1998.
"Fortunately, the most serious shortcomings of the nation's statistical infrastructure could be substantially improved by a limited number of initiatives," the plan added.
The newly released budget plan seeks, among other things, funding to explore improvements to the Consumer Price Index.
The plan seeks increases in the budgets of key agencies, like the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) and the Commerce Department Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA).
BLS, which compiles the consumer and producer price reports and the monthly employment report, would receive a five percent increase in its fiscal 1998 budget.
The proposals to improve CPI would allow BLS to explore the potential for accelerating revisions to the index and to study possible alternative measures for the cost of living.
It would also allow the agency to look at ways to improve measurement of the quality change of goods and services and to bring new items into the index more rapidly.
The request for money to improve the CPI follows a report by a congressionally appointed panel that concluded the index overstates inflation by 1.1 percentage points a year.

The commission recommended allocating money to make technical changes to the CPI but also suggested Congress consider legislation to change the way it indexes federal taxes benefit programs for cost of living changes.
In the budget, the administration said any changes to the CPI should be "studied carefully and justified thoroughly."

Concerning the budget for BEA, which produces the gross domestic product statistics, the administration requests a 15 percent rise in the budget to allow it to implement the next steps in its plan to improve measurement of output and prices and help better measure investment, savings and wealth.
